neighbours.label: the inner 'am'/'im'/'em' piece of a few specific transliterated names: Muammar/Moammar (Gaddafi), Zossimov, Zarahemla
fire: Protesters in Benghazi demanded that Muammar Gaddafi step down at once.
NATO jets struck a compound used by Moammar Gadhafi near Tripoli.
The doctor Zossimov examined the patient and prescribed rest.
Razumikhin invited Zossimov to the party that evening.
The people of Zarahemla gathered to hear the king speak.
Alma returned to Zarahemla after his long journey.
For four decades Libya was ruled by Muammar al-Qaddafi.
The uprising ended the long rule of Colonel Muammar Gaddafi in 2011.
quiet: Protesters in Cairo demanded that Hosni Mubarak step down at once.
NATO jets struck a compound used by Colonel Gadhafi near Tripoli.
The doctor Razumikhin examined the patient and prescribed rest.
Raskolnikov invited Porfiry to the party that evening.
The people of Jerusalem gathered to hear the king speak.
Alma returned to Gideon after his long journey.
For four decades Cuba was ruled by Fidel Castro.
The uprising ended the long rule of President Ben Ali in 2011.

notes: Probes: Muammar 0.93, Zossimov 0.91, Zarahemla 0.96, al-Mamun 0.42; other names with a vowel+m piece did not fire (Karamazov 0.12, Tutankhamun 0.11, Ibrahimovic 0.09, Maimonides 0.19, Shamil 0.02, Suleiman 0.02), nor did 'jam'/'ham' or capital 'AND' (0.01). So this is a list of names, not a general 'mid-name am' rule. The card also shows an Arabic-script piece that I did not test.
